grading: Evaluator manually inspected every requested material fact and summary evidence against the predetermined unchanged key. Confidence/support labels are evidence, not automatic grades. Simple arithmetic and direct application count as supported.

grades.question: Set up a two-player game. How many tokens of each gem color and how many gold tokens remain, how many nobles are revealed, and what happens to unrevealed nobles?
grades.expected_answer: 4 of each gem color (remove 3 each). All 5 gold remain. Reveal 3 nobles. Unused nobles are removed and will not be used.
material_facts: 4 of each gem color (remove 3 each).
All 5 gold remain.
Reveal 3 nobles.
Unused nobles are removed and will not be used.
grades.observed_answer: Keep 4 tokens of each gem color and all 5 gold tokens. Reveal 3 nobles. Remove the other nobles from the game permanently.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 players: 4 gems per color, 5 gold, 3 nobles. Setup: 'Remove remaining noble tiles from the game -- they will not be used.'
grades.reason: Setup counts and unused-noble destination match the source and summary table.

grades.question: For three players, give the gem-token count per color, gold-token count and noble count. How do those counts differ in a four-player game?
grades.expected_answer: Three: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.
material_facts: Three: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles.
Four: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.
grades.observed_answer: Three players use 5 gems per color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. Four players use 7 gems per color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more gems per color and one more noble, with gold unchanged.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count lists 3: 5 / 5 / 4 and 4: 7 / 5 / 5.
grades.reason: Both player-count configurations, including unchanged gold, are correct.

grades.question: Describe how the development decks and market are prepared: shuffling, order of the three levels, and face-up card counts. Who starts and in which direction does play proceed?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle each deck separately. Place decks in a column increasing bottom to top (1,2,3). Reveal 4 per level, 12 total. Youngest starts; play clockwise.
material_facts: Shuffle each deck separately.
Place decks in a column increasing bottom to top (1,2,3).
Reveal 4 per level, 12 total.
Youngest starts; play clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Shuffle the three level decks separately. Arrange them in a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 on top. Reveal four cards per level for a 3-by-4 market. The youngest player starts, and play goes clockwise.
grades.summary_evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player: 'The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise.'
grades.reason: All deck preparation, market-count, start-player and direction parts are covered.

grades.question: List all four action choices on a turn. May you take gems and then buy a card on the same turn, or reserve and buy that reserved card on that same turn?
grades.expected_answer: Take 3 gems of different colors. Take 2 same-color gems with 4+ available. Reserve 1 development and take 1 gold if available. Buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development. Exactly one action: neither proposed combination is allowed.
material_facts: Take 3 gems of different colors.
Take 2 same-color gems with 4+ available.
Reserve 1 development and take 1 gold if available.
Buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development.
Exactly one action: neither proposed combination is allowed.
grades.observed_answer: Choose exactly one: take three gems of different colors; take two gems of one color if at least four are in that supply; reserve one card with fewer than three already reserved and take one gold if available; or buy one face-up or previously reserved card. You cannot take gems then buy, or reserve then buy that card, on the same turn.
grades.summary_evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of the four listed actions; purchasing includes a card 'reserved on a previous turn.'
grades.reason: All four legal choices, their listed conditions and one-action prohibition are covered.

grades.question: What information about tokens you own must be visible to other players, and when?
grades.expected_answer: All tokens owned by a player must be visible to all players at all times.
material_facts: All tokens owned by a player must be visible to all players at all times.
grades.observed_answer: All tokens you own must be visible to every player at all times.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.'
grades.reason: All owned tokens must remain visible to all players at all times.

grades.question: A green pile contains four tokens; a red pile contains three. Can you take two green, leaving two? Can you take two red? When is the supply threshold checked, and can either gem-taking action take gold?
grades.expected_answer: Two green legal: threshold checked before taking; 4 available suffices. Two red illegal: fewer than 4. Neither gem-taking action obtains gold; only reserving does.
material_facts: Two green legal: threshold checked before taking; 4 available suffices.
Two red illegal: fewer than 4.
Neither gem-taking action obtains gold; only reserving does.
grades.observed_answer: You may take two green from four, leaving two. You may not take two red from three. Check the four-token threshold before taking the tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.
grades.summary_evidence: Turn Structure: 'at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them'; both gem-taking actions specify 'no gold.'
grades.reason: The pre-draw four-token threshold and gold exclusion are correctly applied.

grades.question: You begin with nine tokens and take three different gems. Is temporarily holding twelve allowed, how many must you return, can they include the gems just drawn, and does gold count toward the limit?
grades.expected_answer: Limit applies at end of turn, so temporary twelve allowed. Return 2 to reach 10. May return some or all newly drawn tokens. Gold counts.
material_facts: Limit applies at end of turn, so temporary twelve allowed.
Return 2 to reach 10.
May return some or all newly drawn tokens.
Gold counts.
grades.observed_answer: Temporarily holding twelve is allowed. Return two tokens of your choice to finish with ten; these may include tokens just drawn. Gold counts toward the limit.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Hand Limit permits temporarily exceeding 10, requires returning tokens to exactly 10, includes gold, and allows returning newly taken tokens.
grades.reason: Temporary excess, return of two, newly drawn tokens and gold inclusion are covered.

grades.question: You have ten tokens and fewer than three reserved cards. You reserve a card while gold is available. What happens to the gold and your token count, and what if the gold supply were empty instead?
grades.expected_answer: Take 1 gold with reservation then return 1 chosen token to reach 10 at end. May return the gold just drawn. If no gold, still reserve but receive none; with ten tokens no excess is created.
material_facts: Take 1 gold with reservation then return 1 chosen token to reach 10 at end.
May return the gold just drawn.
If no gold, still reserve but receive none; with ten tokens no excess is created.
grades.observed_answer: Take the gold, temporarily reaching eleven tokens, then return one token of your choice, including that gold if desired, to end with ten. If the gold supply is empty, you may still reserve, receive no gold and remain at ten tokens.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserve: 'If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold.' Token Hand Limit allows returning gold obtained by reserving.
grades.reason: Reservation gold and end-turn limit are combined correctly, including empty-gold exception.

grades.question: From which two places may you reserve a card? If reserving from a deck, which card is taken and is it shown to opponents? Who may eventually buy a reserved card?
grades.expected_answer: A face-up card from the market, or top card of any of the 3 decks. Deck card is taken without showing others. Only the holding player may buy it.
material_facts: A face-up card from the market, or top card of any of the 3 decks.
Deck card is taken without showing others.
Only the holding player may buy it.
grades.observed_answer: Reserve either a face-up market card or the top card from any of the three level decks. A deck reservation is taken without showing opponents. Only the reserving player may buy it.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserve a Development Card lists face-up cards or 'The top card' of any level deck 'without revealing it'; reserved cards may only be purchased by their reserver.
grades.reason: Both reservation sources, top-card privacy and purchaser restriction are correct.

grades.question: You already have three reserved cards and want a fourth, or just want the gold from reserving. Can you reserve now? May you discard or exchange a reserved card to make room, and how can a reserved card leave your hand?
grades.expected_answer: Cannot reserve while holding 3, including to obtain gold. Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card. Only buying it removes it from hand.
material_facts: Cannot reserve while holding 3, including to obtain gold.
Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card.
Only buying it removes it from hand.
grades.observed_answer: You cannot reserve a fourth card, even just to get gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; purchasing it is the only way it leaves your hand.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserved Cards: 'Maximum of 3'; 'The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it.'
grades.reason: Three-card limit, no gold-only reservation, no discard/exchange and purchase-only exit are covered.

grades.question: You reserve a face-up level-2 card while that deck has cards left. When and from where is the empty market space refilled? How does this differ when purchasing a face-up card, buying a reserved card, or when the relevant deck is empty?
grades.expected_answer: Face-up reservation immediately replaced from same-level deck. Face-up purchase has same replacement. Buying from hand does not remove a market card so causes no refill. Empty deck leaves market gap empty, fewer than 4 allowed.
material_facts: Face-up reservation immediately replaced from same-level deck.
Face-up purchase has same replacement.
Buying from hand does not remove a market card so causes no refill.
Empty deck leaves market gap empty, fewer than 4 allowed.
grades.observed_answer: Immediately refill the reserved level-2 card's space with the top card of the level-2 deck. A face-up purchase uses the same immediate replacement rule. Buying a reserved card removes no market card, so creates no market space to refill. If the relevant deck is empty, an emptied market space remains empty for the rest of the game.
grades.summary_evidence: Card Replacement: 'Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced' from the same level; an empty deck leaves the space empty.
grades.reason: Immediate same-level refill, both face-up actions, no hand-purchase refill and depleted deck are covered.

grades.question: A card costs two blue and one green. You have two blue bonuses and no green bonus. What tokens must you spend? What if your bonuses cover every required color, and are bonuses spent when used?
grades.expected_answer: Spend only 1 green. If all costs covered, purchase for zero tokens. Bonuses remain as discounts on later purchases, not spent.
material_facts: Spend only 1 green.
If all costs covered, purchase for zero tokens.
Bonuses remain as discounts on later purchases, not spent.
grades.observed_answer: Spend one green token; the two blue bonuses cover the blue cost. If bonuses cover every cost, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules give this exact blue/green example, call bonuses permanent, and allow purchase 'without spending any tokens at all.'
grades.reason: Discount calculation, free purchase and persistent bonuses are correct.

grades.question: A card costs three blue, two black and one white. You have two blue bonuses, one black bonus, and no white bonus; your available payment is one blue token and two gold. Can you buy it? State which costs the tokens cover, where all spent tokens go, and whether your bonus cards stay with you.
grades.expected_answer: Yes: after bonuses remaining cost is 1 blue,1 black,1 white. Pay blue for blue and two gold for black and white. All spent tokens including gold return to middle supply. Keep bonus cards.
material_facts: Yes: after bonuses remaining cost is 1 blue,1 black,1 white.
Pay blue for blue and two gold for black and white.
All spent tokens including gold return to middle supply.
Keep bonus cards.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Bonuses leave a cost of one blue, one black and one white. Pay the blue token for blue and one gold each for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Your purchased bonus cards stay with you.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce tokens spent; gold substitutes for any single gem; spent gems and gold return to supply. Bonus Stacking calls card bonuses permanent.
grades.reason: Residual cost and all three payments are correct; all spent tokens return and bonus cards stay.

grades.question: Which cards can you purchase with a buy action? After purchase, how should acquired development cards be arranged, and which information on them must always remain visible?
grades.expected_answer: Buy 1 face-up market card or own card reserved on previous turn. Place acquired cards before player sorted into distinct color rows, staggered vertically. Bonuses and prestige point values visible to everyone at all times.
material_facts: Buy 1 face-up market card or own card reserved on previous turn.
Place acquired cards before player sorted into distinct color rows, staggered vertically.
Bonuses and prestige point values visible to everyone at all times.
grades.observed_answer: Buy a face-up market card or a card you reserved previously. Place purchased cards face-up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so everyone can always see their bonuses and prestige values.
grades.summary_evidence: Purchase a Development Card specifies the two sources and says cards are 'sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times.'
grades.reason: Both legal purchase sources, sorted staggered display and continuous visibility are covered.

grades.question: A noble requires three blue, three green and three white bonuses. You have three blue cards, three green cards, two white cards and a white token (or a gold token). Do you qualify? What changes if you instead acquire a third white bonus, and do bonuses above a requirement disqualify you?
grades.expected_answer: No: gem/gold tokens cannot replace bonus requirements. Third white bonus qualifies at end of own turn. Requirements are minimums; excess fine.
material_facts: No: gem/gold tokens cannot replace bonus requirements.
Third white bonus qualifies at end of own turn.
Requirements are minimums; excess fine.
grades.observed_answer: You do not qualify with only two white bonuses; a white or gold token cannot replace the missing bonus. A third white bonus qualifies you at the end of your turn, assuming the noble is available. Bonuses above requirements are allowed.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble Visits requires 'at least' the shown bonuses; Noble Tile Mechanics: 'bonuses ... not gem tokens' and 'having more is fine.'
grades.reason: Tokens do not meet noble requirements; a third white bonus qualifies at turn end; excess allowed.

grades.question: At the end of your action you qualify for two nobles. Can you take both, decline all visits, or choose one? Does the visit use another action, how many points does it give, and when is eligibility checked?
grades.expected_answer: Check end of own turn. Must choose 1, cannot take both or decline. Not an action. Noble worth 3 prestige.
material_facts: Check end of own turn.
Must choose 1, cannot take both or decline.
Not an action.
Noble worth 3 prestige.
grades.observed_answer: Choose exactly one noble; you cannot take both or decline all visits. The visit does not use an action, gives three prestige points, and eligibility is checked at the end of your turn after your action.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble visit rules: automatic, not an action, choose one of multiple nobles, at most one per turn, and each worth 3 points.
grades.reason: Own-turn timing, compulsory single choice, no extra action and three points are covered.

grades.question: Once you receive a noble, where is its tile placed, and is it face up or hidden?
grades.expected_answer: Place it face-up in front of the receiving player.
material_facts: Place it face-up in front of the receiving player.
grades.observed_answer: Place the noble tile face-up in front of you.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble visit rules: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.'
grades.reason: Noble tile face-up placement in front of recipient is explicit.

grades.question: In a four-player game, turns run A, B, C, D, with A first. B reaches fifteen prestige points on their turn. Who still takes a turn before the game ends, does A take another turn, and is B guaranteed to win?
grades.expected_answer: C then D still take their turns. A and B do not take another turn; finish current round for equal turns. B not guaranteed to win: highest final prestige wins.
material_facts: C then D still take their turns.
A and B do not take another turn; finish current round for equal turns.
B not guaranteed to win: highest final prestige wins.
grades.observed_answer: C and D still take their turns, then the game ends. A does not take another turn, because everyone then has equal turn counts. B is not guaranteed to win; the highest final prestige total wins.
grades.summary_evidence: End-Game Trigger completes the current round so everyone has the same number of turns; End-of-Game Clarifications says the triggering player may be surpassed.
grades.reason: Only C and D finish the round; no extra turn for A; highest final points decides.

grades.question: You have thirteen prestige points and receive a noble at the end of your turn. What is your new total, does that trigger the end of the game even though you skipped over fifteen, and when is the winner determined?
grades.expected_answer: Total 16, because noble gives 3. Triggers end: 15 reached or exceeded. Finish current round for equal turns, then compare total prestige including nobles.
material_facts: Total 16, because noble gives 3.
Triggers end: 15 reached or exceeded.
Finish current round for equal turns, then compare total prestige including nobles.
grades.observed_answer: Your total becomes sixteen. That triggers the end condition because it is fifteen or more, even though fifteen was skipped. Determine the winner after the current round finishes and all players have equal turn counts.
grades.summary_evidence: Nobles are worth 3; End-Game Trigger: '15 or more'; Determining the Winner uses the most points 'at the end of the final round.'
grades.reason: Noble raises 13 to 16, crosses the threshold, and comparison waits for equal turns.

grades.question: At the end, A has sixteen prestige and ten purchased developments; B has sixteen prestige and nine purchased developments plus three cards still reserved; C has fifteen prestige and only five purchased developments. Who wins and why? Do nobles count toward prestige, and do B’s reserved cards count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker?
grades.expected_answer: B wins: tied highest at 16 with fewer purchased developments (9 vs 10). C loses on points before tiebreak. Noble points count. Reserved cards are not purchased cards, so B has 9 for tiebreak.
material_facts: B wins: tied highest at 16 with fewer purchased developments (9 vs 10).
C loses on points before tiebreak.
Noble points count.
Reserved cards are not purchased cards, so B has 9 for tiebreak.
grades.observed_answer: B wins. A and B tie for highest prestige, and B has fewer purchased developments, nine versus ten. C's fifteen points lose despite fewer cards. Nobles count toward prestige. B's three reserved cards have not been purchased and do not count for this tiebreaker.
grades.summary_evidence: Winner is most prestige; 'Noble tile points count'; tiebreaker is 'fewest development cards' purchased. Reserved cards must be purchased to leave the hand.
grades.reason: B wins tied highest score on nine purchased cards; reserved cards excluded and nobles included.

grades.question: You have reserved cards showing a total of eight prestige points and two white bonuses, but have not bought them. Do those printed points count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and do those bonuses reduce purchase costs or satisfy nobles?
grades.expected_answer: No reserved-card prestige counts before purchase, including for the end-game trigger. Reserved-card bonuses do not discount purchases or satisfy nobles; only acquired cards provide bonuses.
material_facts: No reserved-card prestige counts before purchase, including for the end-game trigger.
Reserved-card bonuses do not discount purchases or satisfy nobles; only acquired cards provide bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Unpurchased reserved cards contribute neither their eight printed points to your score or end trigger nor their two white bonuses to purchase discounts or nobles.
grades.summary_evidence: Prestige Point Sources: points printed on each 'purchased card'; payment bonuses come from 'previously purchased development cards'; noble bonuses come from purchased cards.
grades.reason: Correctly excludes unpurchased reserved cards from prestige, trigger, discounts and noble requirements.

grades.question: You buy a development card with a blue bonus and zero prestige. Do you receive a physical blue token from the supply, does its bonus work for future purchases, and can it help qualify you for a noble despite being worth zero prestige?
grades.expected_answer: Do not receive a physical blue token; a bonus is a purchase discount. The acquired blue bonus discounts future purchases. A zero-prestige acquired card still contributes its bonus to noble qualification.
material_facts: Do not receive a physical blue token; a bonus is a purchase discount.
The acquired blue bonus discounts future purchases.
A zero-prestige acquired card still contributes its bonus to noble qualification.
grades.observed_answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased card's blue bonus permanently reduces future blue purchase costs and can satisfy noble requirements even though the card is worth zero prestige.
grades.summary_evidence: Bonus Stacking: 'Bonuses ... never generate tokens'; each purchased card adds one permanent bonus. Nobles require bonuses, with no prestige requirement stated.
grades.reason: Distinguishes permanent discount from a physical token and applies a zero-prestige bonus to nobles.

grades.question: A face-up development costs one blue and grants a blue bonus. You have no blue bonus, no blue token and no gold. Can its own bonus make this purchase free? Separately, suppose you can pay for a white-bonus development and it gives you the final bonus needed by a noble: does that new bonus count for the noble at the end of this turn, or only next turn?
grades.expected_answer: The unpurchased card cannot discount its own cost; the first purchase is unaffordable. Bonuses used to discount purchases come from previously acquired cards. A bonus acquired by the paid purchase counts for the end-of-this-turn noble check.
material_facts: The unpurchased card cannot discount its own cost; the first purchase is unaffordable.
Bonuses used to discount purchases come from previously acquired cards.
A bonus acquired by the paid purchase counts for the end-of-this-turn noble check.
grades.observed_answer: The card cannot use its own bonus to make its purchase free; discounts come from previously purchased cards, so you cannot pay the blue cost. A newly purchased white bonus does count for a noble at the end of that same turn, because the noble check follows the action.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules: 'previously purchased development cards'; Turn Structure: after the action, check hand limit and then noble visit.
grades.reason: Correctly distinguishes prior bonuses used to pay from a just-purchased bonus counted at the turn-end noble check.

grades.question: A card costs one blue and two green. You have four blue bonuses and no green bonuses. Can the three excess blue bonuses pay any green cost or give you blue tokens as change? What payment is still needed?
grades.expected_answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs. No physical tokens or change are generated. Two green tokens, or gold substituting for them, are still needed.
material_facts: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs.
No physical tokens or change are generated.
Two green tokens, or gold substituting for them, are still needed.
grades.observed_answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs or produce blue tokens as change. The blue cost is covered, but you must still pay two green tokens or equivalent gold substitutes.
grades.summary_evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess in a color provides 'no benefit for that purchase (no "change" is given)' and bonuses never generate tokens; gold substitutes for any gem.
grades.reason: Keeps excess bonuses within color, gives no change and pays remaining green cost with gems or gold.

grades.question: You qualify for two nobles and receive one. Before your next turn nobody acquires the other noble and your purchased cards stay unchanged. Were the bonuses used up by the first noble, and can taking gems on your next turn still lead to receiving the other noble? Can you collect that other noble during an opponent’s intervening turn?
grades.expected_answer: Bonuses are not used up by receiving a noble. Taking gems is an action after which the end-of-own-turn noble check still occurs; receive the remaining qualifying noble then. Cannot collect the second noble during an opponent’s turn.
material_facts: Bonuses are not used up by receiving a noble.
Taking gems is an action after which the end-of-own-turn noble check still occurs; receive the remaining qualifying noble then.
Cannot collect the second noble during an opponent’s turn.
grades.observed_answer: The first noble does not use up your permanent bonuses. If the other noble remains available, taking gems next turn still allows receiving it at that turn's end. You cannot receive it during an opponent's intervening turn; your noble check is at the end of your own turn.
grades.summary_evidence: Bonuses are permanent; Noble Visits: 'At the end of their turn' and other qualifying nobles 'remain available for future turns.'
grades.reason: Keeps bonuses after receiving a noble and applies the next own-turn check after a non-purchase action; rejects off-turn collection.

grades.question: You have no tokens, no purchased developments and no reserved cards. A face-up level-3 development is far too expensive for you to buy. May you reserve it anyway? Do you pay its printed cost when reserving, and do you take gold if available?
grades.expected_answer: May reserve the face-up level-3 card despite not affording a purchase. Do not pay its printed purchase cost to reserve. Take one gold if available.
material_facts: May reserve the face-up level-3 card despite not affording a purchase.
Do not pay its printed purchase cost to reserve.
Take one gold if available.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, you may reserve that level-3 card despite being unable to buy it. Reserving takes the card without paying its printed purchase cost, and gives one gold if available. You have room under the three-card reservation limit.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserve a Development Card allows one face-up development or top card of any level and awards one gold; payment of printed cost appears under the separate Purchase action.
grades.reason: Correctly treats reservation as independent of printed purchase price and level, with gold if available.

grades.question: Instead of reserving a face-up card, you reserve the top card of the level-2 deck while twelve face-up market cards remain. Must any market card be removed or refilled because of that blind reservation, how many market cards remain, and can you take a second card as a replacement in your hand?
grades.expected_answer: No face-up card was removed, so no market removal or refill occurs; twelve market cards remain. The reserve action gives only one reserved card, not a second replacement card.
material_facts: No face-up card was removed, so no market removal or refill occurs; twelve market cards remain.
The reserve action gives only one reserved card, not a second replacement card.
grades.observed_answer: No market card is removed or refilled. All twelve market cards remain. You take only the single reserved top card, with no second card as a replacement in your hand.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserve says 'Take one development card' and permits a top-deck card. Replacement applies when a face-up card is purchased or reserved 'from the grid.'
grades.reason: Blind draw removes no face-up card and gives only one reserved card; all twelve market cards remain.

grades.question: A level deck has run out, but its four face-up cards are still in the market. Must those cards be removed, or may they still be purchased or reserved? If one is purchased, what happens to that space and to the other three cards?
grades.expected_answer: Keep the four remaining face-up cards available to purchase or reserve. After one is purchased its gap stays empty because the same-level deck is empty. Other three face-up cards remain available.
material_facts: Keep the four remaining face-up cards available to purchase or reserve.
After one is purchased its gap stays empty because the same-level deck is empty.
Other three face-up cards remain available.
grades.observed_answer: The four face-up cards stay available for purchase or reservation. Purchasing one leaves its space empty permanently because the deck is exhausted; the other three remain available.
grades.summary_evidence: Purchase and Reserve allow face-up cards; Card Replacement: 'If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game.'
grades.reason: Retains remaining face-up cards after deck exhaustion and leaves only the vacated space empty.

grades.question: All development decks and face-up market cards have been exhausted; nobody has reached fifteen prestige. A player still has an affordable reserved card and gems are available in at least three colors. Does exhaustion itself end the game? May that player buy the reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action?
grades.expected_answer: Exhausting cards is not the game-end trigger; the source trigger is fifteen prestige followed by completing the round. May buy the affordable own reserved card. May instead take three different gems under the stated available supply; still only one action.
material_facts: Exhausting cards is not the game-end trigger; the source trigger is fifteen prestige followed by completing the round.
May buy the affordable own reserved card.
May instead take three different gems under the stated available supply; still only one action.
grades.observed_answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy the affordable reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action, since those legal actions remain available. Continue until the prestige end condition.
grades.summary_evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'Exhausting the development decks or the face-up market does not end the game. Continue with the remaining legal actions, including purchasing reserved cards.'
grades.reason: Correctly continues remaining legal actions after exhaustion; uses the normal prestige trigger.

grades.question: You already own ten tokens. Three different gem colors are available. Can you take one of each and then return all three newly taken tokens, ending with exactly the same token holdings? Is a net gain of tokens required?
grades.expected_answer: May perform the three-different-gems action, temporarily hold thirteen, then return all three drawn tokens. End with ten; the source explicitly allows returning all newly drawn tokens and imposes no net-gain requirement.
material_facts: May perform the three-different-gems action, temporarily hold thirteen, then return all three drawn tokens.
End with ten; the source explicitly allows returning all newly drawn tokens and imposes no net-gain requirement.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Take one gem from each of three different colors, temporarily hold thirteen, then return all three newly taken gems to end with the same ten tokens. No net token gain is required.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Hand Limit: a player may temporarily exceed 10 and 'may return some or all of the tokens they just took.'
grades.reason: Applies explicit permission to return all newly drawn tokens, including a zero-net-gain action at the limit.

grades.question: The gold supply is empty. On A’s turn, A pays two gold while purchasing a card. B then reserves a card with fewer than three cards reserved. Are A’s spent gold tokens removed from the game, or can B take one, and how many gold tokens are left in the supply immediately after B’s reservation before any token-limit returns?
grades.expected_answer: A returns both gold tokens to the central supply, not out of the game. B takes one available gold with the reservation. One gold remains in supply before any limit returns.
material_facts: A returns both gold tokens to the central supply, not out of the game.
B takes one available gold with the reservation.
One gold remains in supply before any limit returns.
grades.observed_answer: A's two spent gold tokens return to the supply. B takes one when reserving, leaving one gold in the supply immediately afterward, before any token-limit returns.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules: 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'; reserving takes '1 gold token' if available.
grades.reason: Circulates spent gold through the supply to the next reservation and computes the one remaining gold.

grades.question: You have bought no level-1 or level-2 developments, but can pay for a face-up level-3 card. May you purchase that level-3 card now, or must you unlock its level by buying lower-level cards first?
grades.expected_answer: May purchase the affordable face-up level-3 card. The purchase rule imposes no lower-level-card prerequisite; it allows a face-up development from the market.
material_facts: May purchase the affordable face-up level-3 card.
The purchase rule imposes no lower-level-card prerequisite; it allows a face-up development from the market.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. If you can pay, you may purchase a face-up level-3 card immediately; the purchase rule does not require buying lower-level cards first.
grades.summary_evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card.' No level prerequisite is imposed.
grades.reason: Uses the unrestricted face-up-card purchase rule, without inventing lower-level prerequisites.

grades.question: You have twelve prestige, then purchase a three-prestige development whose bonus also makes you qualify for a noble. May you stop at fifteen and skip the noble visit? What is your total after your turn, and can the other players who still have a turn in the round continue playing?
grades.expected_answer: Cannot refuse the qualifying end-of-turn noble even though the purchase reaches fifteen. Total is eighteen after the three-prestige card and three-prestige noble. Complete the current round for equal turns; players with remaining turns still play.
material_facts: Cannot refuse the qualifying end-of-turn noble even though the purchase reaches fifteen.
Total is eighteen after the three-prestige card and three-prestige noble.
Complete the current round for equal turns; players with remaining turns still play.
grades.observed_answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble visit. Your turn ends with eighteen prestige: twelve plus three from the card plus three from the noble. Other players who still have a turn in the current round continue playing before the winner is determined.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble visit is 'automatic' and 'cannot refuse'; nobles worth 3; reaching '15 or more' completes the current round.
grades.reason: Completes compulsory noble acquisition after reaching fifteen, totals eighteen and finishes current round.

grades.question: Four players act A, B, C, D, with A first. D is the first player to reach fifteen prestige on D’s turn. Does A start another round, does everyone get one more turn, or is the game over after D completes this turn? Explain using equal turn counts.
grades.expected_answer: The current round is already complete when D finishes. End after D finishes the turn; A does not start another round and no player gets an extra turn. All players have had equal turn counts.
material_facts: The current round is already complete when D finishes.
End after D finishes the turn; A does not start another round and no player gets an extra turn.
All players have had equal turn counts.
grades.observed_answer: The game ends after D completes the turn. A does not start another round and nobody gets an extra turn, because A, B, C and D have already taken equal numbers of turns when D finishes the current round.
grades.summary_evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete 'the current round' so every player has played 'the same number of turns.'
grades.reason: Recognizes equal turn counts after last player D and adds no extra round.

grades.question: In a two-player game, three nobles were revealed and the other seven removed during setup. After someone receives one noble, do you reveal a new tile from those seven to restore the display to three? Where does the acquired tile go and how many nobles remain available in the middle?
grades.expected_answer: Do not replenish nobles from the seven tiles removed during setup. The acquired noble goes face-up in front of its recipient. Two nobles remain available in the middle.
material_facts: Do not replenish nobles from the seven tiles removed during setup.
The acquired noble goes face-up in front of its recipient.
Two nobles remain available in the middle.
grades.observed_answer: Do not reveal a replacement. The seven removed nobles are permanently out of the game. Put the acquired noble face-up in front of its recipient, leaving two available nobles in the middle.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: tiles removed during setup are 'out of the game permanently'; received nobles go 'face-up in front of you.'
grades.reason: Does not replenish removed nobles; moves acquired tile face up and leaves two available.

grades.question: Match each component name to its color: emerald, diamond, sapphire, onyx, ruby and gold joker. How many development cards are in the box in total and at each of the three levels?
grades.expected_answer: Emerald green; diamond white; sapphire blue; onyx black; ruby red; gold joker yellow. Ninety developments: forty level 1, thirty level 2, twenty level 3.
material_facts: Emerald green; diamond white; sapphire blue; onyx black; ruby red; gold joker yellow.
Ninety developments: forty level 1, thirty level 2, twenty level 3.
grades.observed_answer: Emerald is green, diamond white, sapphire blue, onyx black, ruby red, and gold joker yellow. There are ninety development cards: forty level 1, thirty level 2 and twenty level 3.
grades.summary_evidence: Components token-color table and Development Cards table: 90 total, with levels 1/2/3 containing 40/30/20.
grades.reason: All six token identities and all four development inventory counts match.

grades.question: A card’s remaining cost after bonuses is one green. You hold both one green token and one gold. Must you spend green because you have it, or may you pay gold instead and keep the green? Where does the payment go?
grades.expected_answer: May spend the gold instead; the joker can replace any color, without a requirement that the matching gem be absent. Keep the unused green token; return spent gold to the supply.
material_facts: May spend the gold instead; the joker can replace any color, without a requirement that the matching gem be absent.
Keep the unused green token; return spent gold to the supply.
grades.observed_answer: You may pay the gold and keep your green token. Gold may substitute for any single gem token; the payment goes back to the supply.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules: 'Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token. Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply.'
grades.reason: Permits optional gold substitution despite owning matching gem and returns only the spent gold.

grades.question: Three gem piles contain one red, two blue and three green tokens. Other gem piles are empty. Can the three-different-gems action take one from each of these piles, or does the four-token minimum prohibit it? What would remain in those three piles?
grades.expected_answer: May take one from each of red,blue,green. The four-token prerequisite applies to taking two alike, not the three-different-colors action. Remaining piles: zero red, one blue, two green.
material_facts: May take one from each of red,blue,green.
The four-token prerequisite applies to taking two alike, not the three-different-colors action.
Remaining piles: zero red, one blue, two green.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, take one red, one blue and one green. The four-token minimum applies only to taking two of the same color. The piles then contain zero red, one blue and two green.
grades.summary_evidence: Take 3 Gem Tokens: 'Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles'; the four-token threshold is specified for 'Take 2 Gem Tokens of the Same Color.'
grades.reason: Applies the four-token threshold only to two-alike taking, and correctly computes all remaining piles.

grades.question: You hold a gold token and want to exchange it directly for a red token in the supply without buying a development. Is that a listed action or a permitted use of the joker rule? What use does the summary give gold when purchasing?
grades.expected_answer: No direct gold-for-gem exchange action is provided among the four actions. The joker substitutes for a required gem token when paying for a development, not as a supply-conversion action.
material_facts: No direct gold-for-gem exchange action is provided among the four actions.
The joker substitutes for a required gem token when paying for a development, not as a supply-conversion action.
grades.observed_answer: A direct gold-for-red exchange without buying a card is not one of the four listed actions and is not the purchasing substitution described. Gold substitutes for a gem token when paying to purchase a development card.
grades.summary_evidence: Turn Structure requires exactly one of four actions and lists no exchange action. Gold Token Specifics: gold substitutes for any gem color 'when purchasing a card.'
grades.reason: Rejects a standalone exchange action and confines joker substitution to purchase payment.

grades.question: On your turn you can legally buy a face-up card and can also take three different gems. You want neither benefit. May you simply pass without performing an action, or must you choose one of the four actions? This asks about voluntarily passing with legal actions available, not a state in which all actions are impossible.
grades.expected_answer: Must choose exactly one of the four actions; cannot voluntarily take zero actions while legal actions are available. The source does not provide a voluntary pass action.
material_facts: Must choose exactly one of the four actions; cannot voluntarily take zero actions while legal actions are available.

grades.observed_answer: You must choose and perform one of the four actions. Voluntarily passing with legal actions available is not permitted.
grades.summary_evidence: Turn Structure: 'On their turn, a player must perform exactly one of the following four actions.'
grades.reason: Applies must-perform-exactly-one to voluntary passing while legal actions exist, without extending to source-unresolved all-actions-impossible states.

grades.question: Set up a two-player game. How many tokens of each gem color and how many gold tokens remain, how many nobles are revealed, and what happens to unrevealed nobles?
grades.expected_answer: 4 of each gem color (remove 3 each). All 5 gold remain. Reveal 3 nobles. Unused nobles are removed and will not be used.
material_facts: 4 of each gem color (remove 3 each).
All 5 gold remain.
Reveal 3 nobles.
Unused nobles are removed and will not be used.
grades.observed_answer: Keep 4 gems per color and 5 gold. Reveal 3 nobles; the other 7 are permanently removed.

grades.reason: Setup counts and unused-noble destination match the source and summary table.

grades.question: For three players, give the gem-token count per color, gold-token count and noble count. How do those counts differ in a four-player game?
grades.expected_answer: Three: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.
material_facts: Three: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles.
Four: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.
grades.observed_answer: Three players: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four players: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles: two more gems per color and one more noble.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count table.
grades.reason: Both player-count configurations, including unchanged gold, are correct.

grades.question: Describe how the development decks and market are prepared: shuffling, order of the three levels, and face-up card counts. Who starts and in which direction does play proceed?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle each deck separately. Place decks in a column increasing bottom to top (1,2,3). Reveal 4 per level, 12 total. Youngest starts; play clockwise.
material_facts: Shuffle each deck separately.
Place decks in a column increasing bottom to top (1,2,3).
Reveal 4 per level, 12 total.
Youngest starts; play clockwise.

grades.summary_evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player.
grades.reason: All deck preparation, market-count, start-player and direction parts are covered.

grades.question: List all four action choices on a turn. May you take gems and then buy a card on the same turn, or reserve and buy that reserved card on that same turn?
grades.expected_answer: Take 3 gems of different colors. Take 2 same-color gems with 4+ available. Reserve 1 development and take 1 gold if available. Buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development. Exactly one action: neither proposed combination is allowed.
material_facts: Take 3 gems of different colors.
Take 2 same-color gems with 4+ available.
Reserve 1 development and take 1 gold if available.
Buy 1 face-up or previously reserved development.
Exactly one action: neither proposed combination is allowed.
grades.observed_answer: Take three different gems; take two same-color gems with at least four in that supply; reserve one card if holding fewer than three and take gold if available; or buy one face-up or previously reserved card. Neither taking gems then buying nor reserving then buying that card is allowed in one turn.
grades.summary_evidence: Turn Structure: “must” perform “exactly one” action; reserved purchases require reservation on a previous turn.
grades.reason: Lists the action choices, threshold, reserve limit, purchase sources and gold availability, but abbreviates gold as take gold without the one-token quantity included in the unchanged fixed key. Complete-answer grading requires that material quantity; summary itself already explicitly states one gold. Reader-completeness failure; no summary repair required.

grades.question: What information about tokens you own must be visible to other players, and when?
grades.expected_answer: All tokens owned by a player must be visible to all players at all times.
material_facts: All tokens owned by a player must be visible to all players at all times.
grades.observed_answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.

grades.reason: All owned tokens must remain visible to all players at all times.

grades.question: A green pile contains four tokens; a red pile contains three. Can you take two green, leaving two? Can you take two red? When is the supply threshold checked, and can either gem-taking action take gold?
grades.expected_answer: Two green legal: threshold checked before taking; 4 available suffices. Two red illegal: fewer than 4. Neither gem-taking action obtains gold; only reserving does.
material_facts: Two green legal: threshold checked before taking; 4 available suffices.
Two red illegal: fewer than 4.
Neither gem-taking action obtains gold; only reserving does.
grades.observed_answer: Take two green from four, leaving two. You cannot take two red from three. Check the threshold before taking tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.

grades.reason: The pre-draw four-token threshold and gold exclusion are correctly applied.

grades.question: You begin with nine tokens and take three different gems. Is temporarily holding twelve allowed, how many must you return, can they include the gems just drawn, and does gold count toward the limit?
grades.expected_answer: Limit applies at end of turn, so temporary twelve allowed. Return 2 to reach 10. May return some or all newly drawn tokens. Gold counts.
material_facts: Limit applies at end of turn, so temporary twelve allowed.

May return some or all newly drawn tokens.

grades.observed_answer: Twelve temporarily is allowed. Return two, possibly including newly taken gems. Gold counts toward ten.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Hand Limit allows temporary excess and returning tokens just taken; ten includes gold.
grades.reason: Temporary excess, return of two, newly drawn tokens and gold inclusion are covered.

grades.question: You have ten tokens and fewer than three reserved cards. You reserve a card while gold is available. What happens to the gold and your token count, and what if the gold supply were empty instead?
grades.expected_answer: Take 1 gold with reservation then return 1 chosen token to reach 10 at end. May return the gold just drawn. If no gold, still reserve but receive none; with ten tokens no excess is created.

grades.reason: Reservation gold and end-turn limit are combined correctly, including empty-gold exception.

grades.question: From which two places may you reserve a card? If reserving from a deck, which card is taken and is it shown to opponents? Who may eventually buy a reserved card?
grades.expected_answer: A face-up card from the market, or top card of any of the 3 decks. Deck card is taken without showing others. Only the holding player may buy it.

grades.reason: Both reservation sources, top-card privacy and purchaser restriction are correct.

grades.question: You already have three reserved cards and want a fourth, or just want the gold from reserving. Can you reserve now? May you discard or exchange a reserved card to make room, and how can a reserved card leave your hand?
grades.expected_answer: Cannot reserve while holding 3, including to obtain gold. Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card. Only buying it removes it from hand.
material_facts: Cannot reserve while holding 3, including to obtain gold.
Cannot discard or exchange a reserved card.
Only buying it removes it from hand.

grades.reason: Three-card limit, no gold-only reservation, no discard/exchange and purchase-only exit are covered.

grades.question: You reserve a face-up level-2 card while that deck has cards left. When and from where is the empty market space refilled? How does this differ when purchasing a face-up card, buying a reserved card, or when the relevant deck is empty?
grades.expected_answer: Face-up reservation immediately replaced from same-level deck. Face-up purchase has same replacement. Buying from hand does not remove a market card so causes no refill. Empty deck leaves market gap empty, fewer than 4 allowed.

Face-up purchase has same replacement.
Buying from hand does not remove a market card so causes no refill.
Empty deck leaves market gap empty, fewer than 4 allowed.

grades.summary_evidence: Card Replacement applies immediately to face-up purchases/reservations, from the same level; exhausted deck leaves the space empty.
grades.reason: Immediate same-level refill, both face-up actions, no hand-purchase refill and depleted deck are covered.

grades.question: A card costs two blue and one green. You have two blue bonuses and no green bonus. What tokens must you spend? What if your bonuses cover every required color, and are bonuses spent when used?
grades.expected_answer: Spend only 1 green. If all costs covered, purchase for zero tokens. Bonuses remain as discounts on later purchases, not spent.
material_facts: Spend only 1 green.
If all costs covered, purchase for zero tokens.
Bonuses remain as discounts on later purchases, not spent.
grades.observed_answer: Spend one green and no blue. If bonuses cover everything, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and not spent.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules give this exact blue/green example and allow token-free purchases; bonuses are permanent.
grades.reason: Discount calculation, free purchase and persistent bonuses are correct.

grades.question: A card costs three blue, two black and one white. You have two blue bonuses, one black bonus, and no white bonus; your available payment is one blue token and two gold. Can you buy it? State which costs the tokens cover, where all spent tokens go, and whether your bonus cards stay with you.
grades.expected_answer: Yes: after bonuses remaining cost is 1 blue,1 black,1 white. Pay blue for blue and two gold for black and white. All spent tokens including gold return to middle supply. Keep bonus cards.
material_facts: Yes: after bonuses remaining cost is 1 blue,1 black,1 white.
Pay blue for blue and two gold for black and white.
All spent tokens including gold return to middle supply.
Keep bonus cards.

grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules: bonus discounts, gold substitutes for any gem, spent tokens return to supply; Bonus Stacking: permanent bonuses.
grades.reason: Residual cost and all three payments are correct; all spent tokens return and bonus cards stay.

grades.question: Which cards can you purchase with a buy action? After purchase, how should acquired development cards be arranged, and which information on them must always remain visible?
grades.expected_answer: Buy 1 face-up market card or own card reserved on previous turn. Place acquired cards before player sorted into distinct color rows, staggered vertically. Bonuses and prestige point values visible to everyone at all times.
material_facts: Buy 1 face-up market card or own card reserved on previous turn.
Place acquired cards before player sorted into distinct color rows, staggered vertically.
Bonuses and prestige point values visible to everyone at all times.
grades.observed_answer: Purchase a face-up market card or your previously reserved card. Place purchased cards face-up before you, grouped by bonus color and staggered with bonuses and prestige values always visible to everyone.
grades.summary_evidence: Purchase a Development Card, including the final arrangement paragraph.
grades.reason: Both legal purchase sources, sorted staggered display and continuous visibility are covered.

grades.question: A noble requires three blue, three green and three white bonuses. You have three blue cards, three green cards, two white cards and a white token (or a gold token). Do you qualify? What changes if you instead acquire a third white bonus, and do bonuses above a requirement disqualify you?
grades.expected_answer: No: gem/gold tokens cannot replace bonus requirements. Third white bonus qualifies at end of own turn. Requirements are minimums; excess fine.
material_facts: No: gem/gold tokens cannot replace bonus requirements.
Third white bonus qualifies at end of own turn.
Requirements are minimums; excess fine.
grades.observed_answer: No: tokens, including gold, cannot replace the missing white bonus. A third white bonus qualifies you at the end of your turn. Excess bonuses do not disqualify you.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble Visits: at least the required bonuses from purchased cards, not tokens.
grades.reason: Tokens do not meet noble requirements; a third white bonus qualifies at turn end; excess allowed.

grades.question: At the end of your action you qualify for two nobles. Can you take both, decline all visits, or choose one? Does the visit use another action, how many points does it give, and when is eligibility checked?
grades.expected_answer: Check end of own turn. Must choose 1, cannot take both or decline. Not an action. Noble worth 3 prestige.
material_facts: Check end of own turn.
Must choose 1, cannot take both or decline.
Not an action.
Noble worth 3 prestige.
grades.observed_answer: Choose one noble. You cannot take both or refuse all. It uses no action, gives three prestige, and eligibility is checked at the end of your turn after the action.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble visit rules: automatic, not an action, choose one if multiple, at most one per turn, three points.
grades.reason: Own-turn timing, compulsory single choice, no extra action and three points are covered.

grades.question: Once you receive a noble, where is its tile placed, and is it face up or hidden?
grades.expected_answer: Place it face-up in front of the receiving player.
material_facts: Place it face-up in front of the receiving player.
grades.observed_answer: Place it face-up in front of you.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble Visits: “Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.”
grades.reason: Noble tile face-up placement in front of recipient is explicit.

grades.question: In a four-player game, turns run A, B, C, D, with A first. B reaches fifteen prestige points on their turn. Who still takes a turn before the game ends, does A take another turn, and is B guaranteed to win?
grades.expected_answer: C then D still take their turns. A and B do not take another turn; finish current round for equal turns. B not guaranteed to win: highest final prestige wins.
material_facts: C then D still take their turns.
A and B do not take another turn; finish current round for equal turns.
B not guaranteed to win: highest final prestige wins.
grades.observed_answer: C and D still act; A does not act again. B is not guaranteed to win because another player can surpass B during the final round.
grades.summary_evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round for equal turns. End-of-Game Clarifications: triggering player may be surpassed.
grades.reason: Only C and D finish the round; no extra turn for A; highest final points decides.

grades.question: You have thirteen prestige points and receive a noble at the end of your turn. What is your new total, does that trigger the end of the game even though you skipped over fifteen, and when is the winner determined?
grades.expected_answer: Total 16, because noble gives 3. Triggers end: 15 reached or exceeded. Finish current round for equal turns, then compare total prestige including nobles.
material_facts: Total 16, because noble gives 3.
Triggers end: 15 reached or exceeded.
Finish current round for equal turns, then compare total prestige including nobles.
grades.observed_answer: You reach sixteen and trigger the ending because the threshold is fifteen or more. Determine the winner after the current round is complete and turn counts are equal.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble value three; End-Game Trigger: “15 or more”; winner uses final-round totals.
grades.reason: Noble raises 13 to 16, crosses the threshold, and comparison waits for equal turns.

grades.question: At the end, A has sixteen prestige and ten purchased developments; B has sixteen prestige and nine purchased developments plus three cards still reserved; C has fifteen prestige and only five purchased developments. Who wins and why? Do nobles count toward prestige, and do B’s reserved cards count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker?
grades.expected_answer: B wins: tied highest at 16 with fewer purchased developments (9 vs 10). C loses on points before tiebreak. Noble points count. Reserved cards are not purchased cards, so B has 9 for tiebreak.
material_facts: B wins: tied highest at 16 with fewer purchased developments (9 vs 10).
C loses on points before tiebreak.
Noble points count.
Reserved cards are not purchased cards, so B has 9 for tiebreak.
grades.observed_answer: B wins: A and B tie at sixteen and B bought nine developments versus ten. C has fewer points. Noble points count. B’s reserved cards are not purchased cards and do not enter the tiebreaker.
grades.summary_evidence: Determining the Winner; Tiebreaker uses purchased developments; Prestige Point Sources includes purchased cards and nobles.
grades.reason: B wins tied highest score on nine purchased cards; reserved cards excluded and nobles included.

grades.question: You have reserved cards showing a total of eight prestige points and two white bonuses, but have not bought them. Do those printed points count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and do those bonuses reduce purchase costs or satisfy nobles?
grades.expected_answer: No reserved-card prestige counts before purchase, including for the end-game trigger. Reserved-card bonuses do not discount purchases or satisfy nobles; only acquired cards provide bonuses.
material_facts: No reserved-card prestige counts before purchase, including for the end-game trigger.
Reserved-card bonuses do not discount purchases or satisfy nobles; only acquired cards provide bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Reserved points count toward neither score nor the trigger; their bonuses neither discount purchases nor satisfy nobles until purchased.
grades.summary_evidence: Prestige Point Sources: purchased cards. Payment rules: previously purchased cards. Noble Visits: purchased-card bonuses.
grades.reason: Correctly excludes unpurchased reserved cards from prestige, trigger, discounts and noble requirements.

grades.question: You buy a development card with a blue bonus and zero prestige. Do you receive a physical blue token from the supply, does its bonus work for future purchases, and can it help qualify you for a noble despite being worth zero prestige?
grades.expected_answer: Do not receive a physical blue token; a bonus is a purchase discount. The acquired blue bonus discounts future purchases. A zero-prestige acquired card still contributes its bonus to noble qualification.
material_facts: Do not receive a physical blue token; a bonus is a purchase discount.
The acquired blue bonus discounts future purchases.
A zero-prestige acquired card still contributes its bonus to noble qualification.
grades.observed_answer: No physical blue token is gained. Its permanent blue bonus discounts future purchases and helps qualify for nobles even with zero prestige.
grades.summary_evidence: Cards may be worth zero; Bonus Stacking: bonuses never generate tokens; nobles use purchased-card bonuses.
grades.reason: Distinguishes permanent discount from a physical token and applies a zero-prestige bonus to nobles.

grades.question: A face-up development costs one blue and grants a blue bonus. You have no blue bonus, no blue token and no gold. Can its own bonus make this purchase free? Separately, suppose you can pay for a white-bonus development and it gives you the final bonus needed by a noble: does that new bonus count for the noble at the end of this turn, or only next turn?
grades.expected_answer: The unpurchased card cannot discount its own cost; the first purchase is unaffordable. Bonuses used to discount purchases come from previously acquired cards. A bonus acquired by the paid purchase counts for the end-of-this-turn noble check.
material_facts: The unpurchased card cannot discount its own cost; the first purchase is unaffordable.
Bonuses used to discount purchases come from previously acquired cards.
A bonus acquired by the paid purchase counts for the end-of-this-turn noble check.
grades.observed_answer: You cannot buy the blue card: its own bonus is not from a previously purchased card and cannot pay its cost. A newly bought white bonus counts toward a noble at the end of this same turn.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules: previously purchased cards. Noble Visits: purchased-card bonuses checked at end of turn.
grades.reason: Correctly distinguishes prior bonuses used to pay from a just-purchased bonus counted at the turn-end noble check.

grades.question: A card costs one blue and two green. You have four blue bonuses and no green bonuses. Can the three excess blue bonuses pay any green cost or give you blue tokens as change? What payment is still needed?
grades.expected_answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs. No physical tokens or change are generated. Two green tokens, or gold substituting for them, are still needed.
material_facts: Excess blue bonuses cannot pay green costs.
No physical tokens or change are generated.
Two green tokens, or gold substituting for them, are still needed.
grades.observed_answer: Excess blue bonuses cannot cover green or yield change. You still owe two green, paid with green tokens and/or two equivalent gold substitutions.
grades.summary_evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess bonuses give no benefit for that purchase and no change. Gold substitutes for any single gem.
grades.reason: Keeps excess bonuses within color, gives no change and pays remaining green cost with gems or gold.

grades.question: You qualify for two nobles and receive one. Before your next turn nobody acquires the other noble and your purchased cards stay unchanged. Were the bonuses used up by the first noble, and can taking gems on your next turn still lead to receiving the other noble? Can you collect that other noble during an opponent’s intervening turn?
grades.expected_answer: Bonuses are not used up by receiving a noble. Taking gems is an action after which the end-of-own-turn noble check still occurs; receive the remaining qualifying noble then. Cannot collect the second noble during an opponent’s turn.
material_facts: Bonuses are not used up by receiving a noble.
Taking gems is an action after which the end-of-own-turn noble check still occurs; receive the remaining qualifying noble then.
Cannot collect the second noble during an opponent’s turn.
grades.observed_answer: Bonuses are not used up. Taking gems next turn can still yield the other noble at the end of your turn if it remains available. You cannot receive it on an opponent’s intervening turn.
grades.summary_evidence: Bonuses are permanent; unchosen nobles remain for future turns; visits occur at the end of the player’s turn.
grades.reason: Keeps bonuses after receiving a noble and applies the next own-turn check after a non-purchase action; rejects off-turn collection.

grades.question: You have no tokens, no purchased developments and no reserved cards. A face-up level-3 development is far too expensive for you to buy. May you reserve it anyway? Do you pay its printed cost when reserving, and do you take gold if available?
grades.expected_answer: May reserve the face-up level-3 card despite not affording a purchase. Do not pay its printed purchase cost to reserve. Take one gold if available.
material_facts: May reserve the face-up level-3 card despite not affording a purchase.
Do not pay its printed purchase cost to reserve.
Take one gold if available.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, reserve it despite being unable to buy it. Reserving does not require paying the printed purchase cost. Take one gold if available.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserve a Development Card permits face-up cards without a cost payment; payment belongs to the separate purchase action.
grades.reason: Correctly treats reservation as independent of printed purchase price and level, with gold if available.

grades.question: Instead of reserving a face-up card, you reserve the top card of the level-2 deck while twelve face-up market cards remain. Must any market card be removed or refilled because of that blind reservation, how many market cards remain, and can you take a second card as a replacement in your hand?
grades.expected_answer: No face-up card was removed, so no market removal or refill occurs; twelve market cards remain. The reserve action gives only one reserved card, not a second replacement card.
material_facts: No face-up card was removed, so no market removal or refill occurs; twelve market cards remain.
The reserve action gives only one reserved card, not a second replacement card.
grades.observed_answer: No market card is removed or replaced; twelve remain. You take only the one deck card into your hand, with no second replacement card.
grades.summary_evidence: Reserve a Development Card: take one card, either face-up or top of a deck. Replacement applies to face-up cards removed from the grid.
grades.reason: Blind draw removes no face-up card and gives only one reserved card; all twelve market cards remain.

grades.question: A level deck has run out, but its four face-up cards are still in the market. Must those cards be removed, or may they still be purchased or reserved? If one is purchased, what happens to that space and to the other three cards?
grades.expected_answer: Keep the four remaining face-up cards available to purchase or reserve. After one is purchased its gap stays empty because the same-level deck is empty. Other three face-up cards remain available.
material_facts: Keep the four remaining face-up cards available to purchase or reserve.
After one is purchased its gap stays empty because the same-level deck is empty.
Other three face-up cards remain available.
grades.observed_answer: The four face-up cards remain available for purchase or reservation. Buying one leaves an empty space because its deck is empty; the other three remain available.
grades.summary_evidence: Purchase/reservation actions allow face-up cards. Card Replacement: exhausted deck leaves the space empty.
grades.reason: Retains remaining face-up cards after deck exhaustion and leaves only the vacated space empty.

grades.question: All development decks and face-up market cards have been exhausted; nobody has reached fifteen prestige. A player still has an affordable reserved card and gems are available in at least three colors. Does exhaustion itself end the game? May that player buy the reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action?
grades.expected_answer: Exhausting cards is not the game-end trigger; the source trigger is fifteen prestige followed by completing the round. May buy the affordable own reserved card. May instead take three different gems under the stated available supply; still only one action.
material_facts: Exhausting cards is not the game-end trigger; the source trigger is fifteen prestige followed by completing the round.
May buy the affordable own reserved card.
May instead take three different gems under the stated available supply; still only one action.
grades.observed_answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy the reserved card or take three different gems. Continue until the normal prestige-point ending.
grades.summary_evidence: End-Game Trigger explicitly states deck or market exhaustion does not end the game; continue remaining legal actions including reserved purchases.
grades.reason: Correctly continues remaining legal actions after exhaustion; uses the normal prestige trigger.

grades.question: You already own ten tokens. Three different gem colors are available. Can you take one of each and then return all three newly taken tokens, ending with exactly the same token holdings? Is a net gain of tokens required?
grades.expected_answer: May perform the three-different-gems action, temporarily hold thirteen, then return all three drawn tokens. End with ten; the source explicitly allows returning all newly drawn tokens and imposes no net-gain requirement.
material_facts: May perform the three-different-gems action, temporarily hold thirteen, then return all three drawn tokens.
End with ten; the source explicitly allows returning all newly drawn tokens and imposes no net-gain requirement.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Take the three and return all three just taken to end with the same ten. No net gain is required.
grades.summary_evidence: Token Hand Limit permits temporary excess and returning “some or all of the tokens they just took.”
grades.reason: Applies explicit permission to return all newly drawn tokens, including a zero-net-gain action at the limit.

grades.question: The gold supply is empty. On A’s turn, A pays two gold while purchasing a card. B then reserves a card with fewer than three cards reserved. Are A’s spent gold tokens removed from the game, or can B take one, and how many gold tokens are left in the supply immediately after B’s reservation before any token-limit returns?
grades.expected_answer: A returns both gold tokens to the central supply, not out of the game. B takes one available gold with the reservation. One gold remains in supply before any limit returns.
material_facts: A returns both gold tokens to the central supply, not out of the game.
B takes one available gold with the reservation.
One gold remains in supply before any limit returns.
grades.observed_answer: A returns the two gold to supply. B takes one on reserving, leaving one gold in supply before token-limit returns.
grades.summary_evidence: Payment rules return spent gold to supply; reservation takes one gold if available.
grades.reason: Circulates spent gold through the supply to the next reservation and computes the one remaining gold.

grades.question: You have bought no level-1 or level-2 developments, but can pay for a face-up level-3 card. May you purchase that level-3 card now, or must you unlock its level by buying lower-level cards first?
grades.expected_answer: May purchase the affordable face-up level-3 card. The purchase rule imposes no lower-level-card prerequisite; it allows a face-up development from the market.
material_facts: May purchase the affordable face-up level-3 card.
The purchase rule imposes no lower-level-card prerequisite; it allows a face-up development from the market.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, buy the affordable face-up level-3 card now. The purchase action has no requirement to acquire lower levels first.
grades.summary_evidence: Purchase a Development Card allows a face-up card from the grid on payment; the grid includes all three levels.
grades.reason: Uses the unrestricted face-up-card purchase rule, without inventing lower-level prerequisites.

grades.question: You have twelve prestige, then purchase a three-prestige development whose bonus also makes you qualify for a noble. May you stop at fifteen and skip the noble visit? What is your total after your turn, and can the other players who still have a turn in the round continue playing?
grades.expected_answer: Cannot refuse the qualifying end-of-turn noble even though the purchase reaches fifteen. Total is eighteen after the three-prestige card and three-prestige noble. Complete the current round for equal turns; players with remaining turns still play.
material_facts: Cannot refuse the qualifying end-of-turn noble even though the purchase reaches fifteen.
Total is eighteen after the three-prestige card and three-prestige noble.
Complete the current round for equal turns; players with remaining turns still play.
grades.observed_answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble. Your turn ends at eighteen points: twelve plus three plus three. Players still due a turn in the current round continue.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble visits cannot be refused and grant three points; End-Game Trigger completes the current round.
grades.reason: Completes compulsory noble acquisition after reaching fifteen, totals eighteen and finishes current round.

grades.question: Four players act A, B, C, D, with A first. D is the first player to reach fifteen prestige on D’s turn. Does A start another round, does everyone get one more turn, or is the game over after D completes this turn? Explain using equal turn counts.
grades.expected_answer: The current round is already complete when D finishes. End after D finishes the turn; A does not start another round and no player gets an extra turn. All players have had equal turn counts.
material_facts: The current round is already complete when D finishes.
End after D finishes the turn; A does not start another round and no player gets an extra turn.
All players have had equal turn counts.
grades.observed_answer: The game ends after D completes this turn. A does not start another round and nobody gets an extra turn, since everyone has taken the same number of turns.
grades.summary_evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round so every player has played the same number of turns.
grades.reason: Recognizes equal turn counts after last player D and adds no extra round.

grades.question: In a two-player game, three nobles were revealed and the other seven removed during setup. After someone receives one noble, do you reveal a new tile from those seven to restore the display to three? Where does the acquired tile go and how many nobles remain available in the middle?
grades.expected_answer: Do not replenish nobles from the seven tiles removed during setup. The acquired noble goes face-up in front of its recipient. Two nobles remain available in the middle.
material_facts: Do not replenish nobles from the seven tiles removed during setup.
The acquired noble goes face-up in front of its recipient.
Two nobles remain available in the middle.
grades.observed_answer: No replacement noble is revealed: removed nobles are permanently out. The acquired tile goes face-up before its recipient. Two nobles remain in the middle.
grades.summary_evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: removed nobles permanently out; Noble Visits: received tile face-up in front of player.
grades.reason: Does not replenish removed nobles; moves acquired tile face up and leaves two available.

grades.question: Match each component name to its color: emerald, diamond, sapphire, onyx, ruby and gold joker. How many development cards are in the box in total and at each of the three levels?
grades.expected_answer: Emerald green; diamond white; sapphire blue; onyx black; ruby red; gold joker yellow. Ninety developments: forty level 1, thirty level 2, twenty level 3.
